messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: paging on-call: p99 spike on streaming endpoints (eu-west-1). Alert: p95 380ms -> 1.8s, p99 1.2s -> 6.5s, error rate for chunked responses increased. Immediate triage required.
Maya (oncall): on it. joining voice. assigning initial triage. :pager:
Raj (eng-sre): grabbing graphs. I see sustained queue depth on proxy pool eu-proxy-03, connections piling in ESTABLISHED with send-Q growth. Few 504s from proxy -> backend. No obvious infra CPU/GPU saturation.
Lin (eng-runtime): checking serving runtime traces. tail latency on streaming RPCs correlates with long stalls in the chunking loop. There's a recent config flip for `chunk_size_v2=true` rolled yesterday in eu canary.
Tomas (eng-platform): rollback canary? We rolled chunk_size_v2 to 30 KB chunks, previously 8 KB. Could be larger chunks + slow clients = head-of-line blocking.
Maya (oncall): priority: mitigate customer impact, then rollback if needed. Which customers impacted? Priya, do we have CS input?
Priya (customer-success): received two escalations from customers in EU region (realtime-search and payments notifications). Both report intermittent stalls during SSE streams; timeouts at ~20s. Customers are on dedicated accounts.
Raj (eng-sre): digging logs. Proxy logs show repeated `write: connection reset by peer` and `client send buffer full` events leading to backpressure. Also `upstream write timeout` entries around same time.
SupportBot: Added incident ticket INC-2026-721, linked runbook streaming-tail-latency.md.
Maya (oncall): steps I want now: 1) throttle large chunk clients at proxy layer, 2) enable fallback routing to smaller-chunk variant, 3) consider rolling back chunk_size_v2 in eu. Raj/Lin you coordinate.
Lin (eng-runtime): I can flip runtime to preserve small chunking per-request via header override `x-chunk-policy: small`. Pushing patch to proxy routing to inject header for eu region for now.
Raj (eng-sre): rolling a hotfix to proxy pods: add `limit_req` on streaming path to throttle concurrent writers and set `proxy_buffering off` for SSE endpoints. Rolling to 2/4 pods first. Command:
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/eu-proxy --selector=canary=false
# apply nginx conf snippet
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 90s;
  limit_req zone=stream burst=20 nodelay;
}
```
Maya (oncall): apply to half the pool, watch p99 for 5m, then continue.
Tomas (eng-platform): tagging traffic route: will bump fallback route weight to 30% to route to legacy-chunk variant svc-legacy-eu. Doing now.
Raj (eng-sre): initial metrics: after hotfix on 2 pods p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 650ms, p99 from 6.5s -> 2.2s. Still above SLO but trending.
Priya (customer-success): notified impacted customers that we're actively mitigating; asked for logs/trace ids. Customers want ETA. I'll give 30m with updates.
Lin (eng-runtime): quick investigation into runtime commit -- nothing blocking except increased tokenization buffer allocator that occasionally yields a 200-500ms stall per chunk for large inputs. That, combined with large chunk sizes, amplifies head-of-line.
Maya (oncall): decision: abort further rollout of chunk_size_v2 in eu and start rollback. Tomas coordinate rollback with infra change window.
Tomas (eng-platform): initiating canary rollback now: `kubectl set env deploy/streaming-runtime CHUNK_SIZE_V2=false` then rolling restarts. Rolling restart command queued. Will move full pool in 10m.
Raj (eng-sre): creating temporary rate-limiting rule by client id for the worst offending clients (top 5 by connection time) to reduce slow consumer impact.
SupportBot: Noted: action items assigned: rollback chunk_size_v2 (Lin/Tomas), proxy hotfix (Raj), contact customers (Priya), monitor (Maya).
Maya (oncall): update: after rolling fallback routing + proxy hotfix + initial partial rollback, p95 420ms, p99 980ms. Still slightly over SLO for some customers but much improved.
Priya (customer-success): customer A (payments) reports streams resumed; customer B (search) still sees occasional 5s stalls but acceptance that we're working.
Lin (eng-runtime): pushing full rollback now. Patch reverted and rolled to all runtime pods in eu. Command: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/streaming-runtime --timeout=10m`
Raj (eng-sre): monitoring shows proxy queue depth normalizing, number of slow consumers dropped ~75%. No new 504 spikes.
Maya (oncall): good. keep watch for 30m. If p99 < 700ms for 30m, we can declare mitigated.
Tomas (eng-platform): will also create a config guard to prevent future large chunk rollout without staged canary with synthetic slow-client test. Filing ticket CFG-1458.
Priya (customer-success): I'll schedule a follow-up with affected customers and offer a postmortem.
Maya (oncall): postmortem owners: Raj (ops), Lin (runtime), Tomas (platform). Runbook updates: add slow-client synthetic tests, add automatic per-client send-queue alerts.
Raj (eng-sre): notes to include in postmortem: observed `send-Q` growth, proxy buffering + large chunks => backpressure, runtime tokenization stalls amplified tail. Mitigation sequence: proxy hotfix (buffering off + limit_req), route to legacy chunk variant, rollback chunk_size_v2.
SupportBot: Incident status -> mitigated (monitoring). Incident ticket updated INC-2026-721 -> status: monitoring.
Maya (oncall): closing the page for now. If you see regressions, ping this thread. Great handling everyone. :thumbsup:
Raj (eng-sre): adding logs we used for triage:
```
# sample proxy log
2026-03-15T17:42:12Z eu-proxy-03 upstream timeout writing to backend id=stream-abc send-Q=65536 client=10.4.5.6
2026-03-15T17:42:15Z eu-proxy-03 client write buffer full client=10.4.5.6 id=stream-abc
```
Lin (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a small regression test to cover large-chunk + slow consumer scenario and add to CI.
Maya (oncall): thanks. I'll update the incident board and schedule the follow-up postmortem meeting.
Priya (customer-success): leaving notes for customers and will join postmortem.
IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-2026-721 moved to monitoring.
Maya (oncall): thread archived after 30m if stable.
